questions.question: A unit whole life annuity-immediate pays at times 1, 2, ... only while its recipient survives. It is issued at time zero. What does being alive at issue guarantee about its payments?
options: No scheduled payment is guaranteed by issue survival alone.
The scheduled payment at issue is guaranteed by issue survival.
The first anniversary payment is guaranteed by issue survival.
The death-year-end payment is guaranteed by issue survival.

questions.question: A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate uses $0<v<1$. Death before year 1 has probability $q>0$, and survival beyond year 1 has positive probability. What can be said about its random present value $Y^*$?
options: It is a continuous variable with no point masses.
It is at least one with probability one.
It is zero only when the discount factor is zero.
It has a positive point mass at zero.

questions.question: Two unit whole life annuities share the same mortality and interest basis. The due version pays at 0, 1, ... while alive; the immediate version pays at 1, 2, ... while alive. What is the realised difference in their present values?
options: The difference equals the discounted first-anniversary payment.
The difference depends on the recipient remaining lifetime.
The immediate value exceeds the due value by exactly one.
The due value exceeds the immediate value by exactly one.

questions.question: A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate uses discount factor $v=0.9$. The recipient dies at time 2.4. What is its realised present value?

A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate has discount factor $v=0.9$ and continuous lifetime $T$. Survival probabilities at years 1 and 2 are $0.8$ and $0.5$. What is the probability its realised present value equals $0.9$?
A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate has discount factor $v=0.9$. Survival probabilities at years 1 and 2 are 0.8 and 0.5; survival to year 3 is zero. What is its APV?
A unit annual whole life annuity-due has present-value variance 4. The matching whole life annuity-immediate omits only the deterministic initial unit. What is its present-value variance?

A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate has annual factor $v=0.9$ and first-year survival probability $p_x=0.8$. Conditional on surviving a year, the remaining annuity-due at age $x+1$ has APV 5. What is the immediate APV at age $x$?

Let $Y$ be the present value of a unit annual whole life annuity-due and $Y^*=Y-1$ that of its matching immediate annuity. Assume finite second moments. Which raw second-moment relation follows despite equal variances?
options: $\mathbb{E}[(Y^*)^2]=\mathbb{E}[Y^2]$.
$\mathbb{E}[(Y^*)^2]=\mathbb{E}[Y^2]-1$.
$\mathbb{E}[(Y^*)^2]=\mathbb{E}[Y^2]-2\mathbb{E}[Y]+1$.

questions.question: At known $0<v<1$, a unit annual whole life annuity-immediate has realised value $Y^*=\sum_{k=1}^Kv^k$, where $K=\lfloor T\rfloor$ and $T$ is continuous remaining lifetime. What information about $T$ does knowing $Y^*$ exactly determine?
options: The integer K, but not the fractional part of T.
The exact death time T, including its fractional part.
Only the mean of K across the mortality population.
Neither K nor any interval containing the death time.

questions.question: At a common mortality and interest basis, let $D$ and $I$ be APVs of unit annual whole life due and immediate annuities, with $0<v<1$. Why is $I=vD$ generally incorrect?
options: Delaying survival payments also changes who survives to receive them.
Discounting cannot be applied to a stream of annual payments.
The immediate contract has an extra guaranteed payment at issue.
Survival probabilities are identical at every annual payment date.

questions.question: For a unit annual whole life annuity-immediate, conditional survival each year is $p=0.8$ and discount factor is $v=0.9$. What is its APV?
A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate is valued at zero interest. The completed remaining lifetime $K$ has finite mean 2. What is the APV?

A life has constant annual survival $p=3/4$, giving completed-year count $K$ with $\mathbb{P}(K=k)=(1-p)p^k$ for $k\ge0$ and $K$ is finite almost surely. A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate uses negative interest with discount factor $v=3/2$. Is its APV finite?
options: Yes; a finite realised payment count guarantees finite APV.
No; the expected payment terms have ratio vp=9/8>1.
Yes; each annual survival probability is below one.
No; negative interest makes every realised payment count infinite.

questions.question: A unit immediate annuity has continuous lifetime $T$ uniform on $(0,1)$, value $Y^*=\sum_{k=1}^{\lfloor T\rfloor}v^k$, and $0<v<1$. An at-death benefit has value $W=v^T$. Is the claimed identity $W+(1-v)Y^*=v$ valid?
options: Yes; $W+(1-v)Y^*=v$ almost surely.
No; $W+(1-v)Y^*<v$ almost surely.
No; $W+(1-v)Y^*>v$ almost surely.
No; $W+(1-v)Y^*=1$ almost surely.

questions.question: A life has continuous remaining lifetime uniform on $(0,1)$. A unit annual whole life annuity-immediate pays at surviving integer anniversaries, with $v=0.9$. A proposed valuation multiplies first-year survival zero by an APV conditional on surviving to year 1. What is the valid conclusion?
options: Own APV is zero; that conditional continuation is undefined.
Own APV is zero; the conditional continuation is necessarily zero.
Own APV is 0.9; mortality before year 1 does not matter.
Own APV is one; the issue payment must be retained.

questions.question: For a unit annual whole life annuity-immediate, let $p_k$ be the survival probability to integer year $k$ and $v>0$ the annual discount factor. Which sum equals its APV for every $v>0$ and every mortality law with finite APV?
options: $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}v^kp_k$.
$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}v^kp_k$.
$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}v^{k-1}p_k$.
$\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}v^k(1-p_k)$.
